domains.name: transaction
domains.description: Core payment transaction processing owning the full lifecycle from authorization, capture, clearing, settlement instruction, and reconciliation. SSOT for all payment events processed through ISO 8583 and ISO 20022 message flows, real-time authorization decisions, batch processing records, TPS metrics, STP rates, and multi-currency transaction data across card-present, card-not-present, and digital payment channels.

products.name: payment_txn
products.description: Core SSOT for every payment transaction processed through the platform — card-present, card-not-present, and digital payment channels. Captures the full ISO 8583 / ISO 20022 message lifecycle from authorization request through capture, including transaction amount, currency, MCC, channel type (POS, mPOS, eCommerce, QR, NFC, HCE), entry mode (EMV, swipe, contactless, manual), transaction timestamp, acquirer reference number (ARN), network transaction ID, processing code, response code, and STP flag. Single authoritative record per payment event.

SSOT for currency conversion events at the transaction level, supporting cross-border payment reporting and DCC revenue tracking.

products.name: txn_type
products.description: Reference classification of payment transaction types supported across the platform — purchase, cash advance, balance inquiry, refund, reversal, pre-authorization, incremental authorization, account verification, P2P transfer, A2A transfer, BNPL installment, ACH debit, ACH credit, RTGS, RTP. Each type record stores the ISO processing code, transaction type code, debit/credit indicator, settlement eligibility, and applicable network rules. Provides standardized classification for transaction reporting and routing logic.

products.name: txn_limit_rule
products.description: Business rule configuration defining transaction-level limits enforced during authorization — single transaction amount limits, daily cumulative limits, velocity limits (count per hour/day), card-present vs card-not-present limits, cross-border transaction limits, and contactless tap limits. Each rule stores the limit type, limit value, limit currency, applicable instrument type, applicable channel, effective date range, and the regulatory or risk basis for the limit (e.g., PSD2 contactless limit, scheme velocity rule). Owned by the transaction domain as these rules are enforced at authorization time.

attributes.business_glossary_term: Automated Clearing House (ACH) Transaction Fee Amount
attributes.description: Fee charged per ACH (bank transfer) transaction processed for the merchant, expressed in the plan's base currency. Typically lower than card transaction fees.

attributes.name: amex_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Separate MDR percentage applied specifically to American Express card transactions, which often have different pricing than Visa/Mastercard, expressed as a decimal.

attributes.name: avs_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged per transaction when Address Verification System (AVS) checks are performed, expressed in the plan's base currency. Helps reduce fraud risk for card-not-present transactions.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Fraud Detection Platform

attributes.name: batch_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged per settlement batch submitted by the merchant, expressed in the plan's base currency. Applies to merchants using batch settlement rather than real-time capture.
attributes.references: Transaction Processing Platform; Merchant Service Agreement

attributes.name: chargeback_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged to the merchant for each chargeback dispute, regardless of outcome, expressed in the plan's base currency. Covers administrative and processing costs.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: contract_term_months
attributes.description: The minimum contract duration in months that the merchant must commit to when assigned this pricing plan. Null for month-to-month plans.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Contract Management Standards

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user or administrator who created this pricing plan record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this pricing plan record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: currency_conversion_markup_percentage
attributes.description: Markup percentage applied to the foreign exchange (FX) rate when Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) is offered to cardholders, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0300 for 3.00% above spot rate).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; FX and DCC Standards

attributes.name: debit_card_rate_percentage
attributes.description: MDR percentage applied specifically to debit card transactions, typically lower than credit card rates due to Regulation II (Durbin Amendment) caps, expressed as a decimal.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Regulation II; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: early_termination_fee_amount
attributes.description: Penalty fee charged if the merchant terminates the agreement before the contract term expires, expressed in the plan's base currency. Null if no early termination penalty applies.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Contract Management Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this pricing plan becomes binding and applicable to assigned merchants. Transactions on or after this date are governed by this plan's terms.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this pricing plan ceases to be valid. Nullable for open-ended plans. Transactions after this date require a new plan assignment.

attributes.name: interchange_markup_percentage
attributes.description: The markup percentage added on top of the actual interchange cost in interchange-plus pricing models (e.g., 0.0050 for 0.50% above interchange). Null for non-interchange-plus models.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Merchant Service Agreement

attributes.name: interchange_passthrough_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether actual interchange fees (IRF) are passed through to the merchant at cost (true) or absorbed into a blended rate (false). True for interchange-plus and cost-plus models.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Interchange Reimbursement Fee Standards

attributes.name: international_transaction_fee_percentage
attributes.description: Additional percentage fee applied to cross-border transactions where the card issuer is in a different country than the merchant, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0100 for 1.00%).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Cross-Border Payment Standards

attributes.name: mdr_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The base percentage rate charged to the merchant per transaction, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0275 for 2.75%). This is the primary revenue component for flat-rate and blended pricing models.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Merchant Service Agreement

attributes.name: merchant_pricing_plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pricing plan. Active plans are available for assignment; inactive plans are no longer offered but may still govern existing merchants; pending plans are under approval; suspended plans are temporarily unavailable; archived plans are historical records only.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System - Pricing Configuration Module

attributes.name: mid_qualified_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The middle MDR percentage tier in tiered pricing models, applied to transactions that partially meet qualification criteria (e.g., keyed-in transactions, rewards cards), expressed as a decimal.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Tiered Pricing Standards

attributes.name: monthly_account_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fixed monthly account maintenance or service fee charged to the merchant, independent of transaction volume, expressed in the plan's base currency.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Payment Processing Platform

attributes.name: monthly_minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: The minimum monthly fee the merchant must pay regardless of transaction volume, expressed in the plan's base currency. If monthly processing fees fall below this threshold, the merchant is charged the difference.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Payment Processing Platform

attributes.name: non_qualified_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The highest MDR percentage tier in tiered pricing models, applied to transactions that fail qualification criteria (e.g., corporate cards, international cards, manually entered), expressed as a decimal.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Tiered Pricing Standards

attributes.name: payfac_sub_merchant_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this pricing plan is available for assignment to sub-merchants under a Payment Facilitator (PayFac) model. True if eligible for PayFac sub-merchants; false if only for direct merchants.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PayFac Program Standards

attributes.name: pci_compliance_fee_amount
attributes.description: Annual or monthly fee charged to merchants for PCI DSS compliance program administration, security scanning, and attestation support, expressed in the plan's base currency.
attributes.references: PCI Security Standards Council; PCI DSS Requirements

attributes.name: pci_non_compliance_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monthly penalty fee charged to merchants who fail to maintain PCI DSS compliance, expressed in the plan's base currency. Escalates with duration of non-compliance.
attributes.references: PCI Security Standards Council; PCI DSS Requirements

attributes.name: per_transaction_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fixed fee charged per transaction in addition to the percentage-based MDR, expressed in the plan's base currency (e.g., 0.10 for $0.10 per transaction).
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Payment Processing Platform

attributes.name: plan_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the pricing plan, used in contracts and merchant communications.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System - Pricing Configuration Module

attributes.name: plan_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the pricing plan, including key features, target merchant segments, and value proposition.
attributes.references: Merchant Management System - Pricing Configuration Module

attributes.name: plan_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the pricing plan (e.g., 'Standard Retail', 'Enterprise Plus', 'Startup Flat Rate').
attributes.references: Merchant Management System - Pricing Configuration Module

attributes.name: pricing_model_type
attributes.description: The fundamental pricing structure applied to merchant transactions. Flat-rate charges a single percentage; interchange-plus passes through interchange costs plus a markup; tiered groups transactions into qualified/mid-qualified/non-qualified buckets; blended averages all transaction types; cost-plus adds a fixed margin to actual costs; custom indicates bespoke negotiated terms.
attributes.references: PCI Security Standards Council; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: qualified_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The lowest MDR percentage tier in tiered pricing models, applied to transactions that meet all qualification criteria (e.g., swiped consumer credit cards), expressed as a decimal.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Tiered Pricing Standards

attributes.name: refund_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged to the merchant for processing a refund or credit transaction, expressed in the plan's base currency. Some plans waive this fee; others charge per refund.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Transaction Processing Platform

attributes.name: retrieval_request_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged to the merchant for each retrieval request (pre-chargeback inquiry) from the issuing bank, expressed in the plan's base currency.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: setup_fee_amount
attributes.description: One-time fee charged when a merchant is onboarded and assigned to this pricing plan, covering account setup, KYC processing, and initial configuration, expressed in the plan's base currency.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Merchant Management System

attributes.name: statement_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged for generating and delivering monthly merchant statements (paper or electronic), expressed in the plan's base currency.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Payment Processing Platform

attributes.name: updated_by_user
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user or administrator who last modified this pricing plan record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this pricing plan record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: voice_authorization_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged when a merchant obtains authorization via phone call to the authorization center rather than electronic authorization, expressed in the plan's base currency.

attributes.name: volume_tier_threshold_amount
attributes.description: Monthly transaction volume threshold (in base currency) that triggers preferential pricing or tier upgrades. Used in volume-based pricing models where rates decrease as volume increases.
attributes.references: Merchant Service Agreement; Payment Processing Platform

products.name: irf_table

Stores interchange rate categories, rate percentages, per-transaction fees, effective dates, card type applicability, transaction type qualifiers, and scheme-specific program identifiers. This is the authoritative SSOT for all interchange rate definitions used in cost-of-acceptance calculations.

attributes.name: interchange_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage rate component of the interchange fee applied to the transaction amount (e.g., 1.65% stored as 0.0165). Used in cost-of-acceptance calculations.

attributes.name: currency_pair_id

attributes.name: participant_id

attributes.name: payment_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: MDR configurations define merchant discount rates for specific payment products (credit cards, debit cards, digital wallets). Acquirers price merchants based on payment product type. Essential for mer

attributes.name: scheme_id

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this MDR configuration applies to Durbin-regulated debit transactions (subject to interchange fee caps under Regulation II).

attributes.name: effective_start_date

attributes.name: tier_3_rate_percent

attributes.name: transaction_channel

attributes.name: merchant_account_id

attributes.name: participant_id

attributes.name: payment_product_id

attributes.name: risk_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_profile. Business justification: Merchant service fee schedules are risk-adjusted. High-risk merchants pay premium fees, early termination fees, and higher chargeback fees. Risk profile drives fee schedule assignment and approval.

attributes.name: annual_fee_amount

attributes.name: avs_fee_amount

attributes.name: chargeback_fee_amount

attributes.name: contract_term_months

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: currency_code

attributes.name: durbin_exempt_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee schedule applies to Durbin Amendment exempt transactions (small issuer or government/reloadable prepaid cards).

attributes.name: early_termination_fee_amount

attributes.name: international_transaction_fee_amount

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: monthly_account_fee_amount

attributes.name: monthly_minimum_fee_amount

attributes.name: msf_schedule_status

attributes.name: notes

products.name: scheme_fee_table
products.description: Card scheme assessment and network fee table capturing all fees levied by Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, and other schemes on acquirers and issuers. Includes assessment rates, network access fees, cross-border fees, digital enablement fees, misuse-of-authorization fees, and scheme-specific surcharges. Effective date ranges and volume tier thresholds are tracked for accurate cost modeling.

attributes.name: scheme_fee_table_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the scheme fee table record.

attributes.name: currency_pair_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.currency_pair. Business justification: Scheme fees are published per currency pair with different rates for domestic vs cross-border transactions. Critical for accurate scheme fee calculation in multi-currency payment processing.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.gl_account. Business justification: Scheme fees are posted to specific expense GL accounts. Fee tables require GL account mapping for automated posting during settlement reconciliation and scheme invoice processing.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Scheme fee tables are published by specific card schemes (Visa, Mastercard). Scheme fee reconciliation, billing audits, and regulatory reporting all require knowing which scheme published each fee tab

attributes.name: volume_tier_threshold_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interchange.volume_tier_threshold. Business justification: scheme_fee_table embeds volume tier bounds (volume_tier_lower_bound, volume_tier_upper_bound, volume_tier_unit) directly on the fee record. The volume_tier_threshold product is the authoritative SSOT

attributes.name: assessment_basis
attributes.description: Basis on which assessment fees are calculated: gross volume (total transaction value including refunds), net volume (purchases minus refunds), or transaction count.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: bin_range_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of BIN/IIN range to which this fee applies. Used for BIN-level interchange qualification rules. Null if fee applies to all BINs.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: bin_range_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of BIN/IIN range to which this fee applies. Used for BIN-level interchange qualification rules. Null if fee applies to all BINs.
attributes.references: ISO 7812; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: card_present_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the fee applies to card-present (POS/mPOS), card-not-present (e-commerce/MOTO), or both transaction environments.

attributes.name: card_product_type
attributes.description: Type of card product to which this fee applies: credit, debit, prepaid, commercial (business/corporate), or all card types.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scheme fee table record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: digital_wallet_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee applies specifically to digital wallet or tokenized transactions (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay). True if digital-wallet-specific, false otherwise.

attributes.name: domestic_international_indicator
attributes.description: Specifies whether the fee applies to domestic transactions (same country acquirer/issuer), international (cross-border), or both.

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee applies to Durbin Amendment regulated debit transactions (US Regulation II compliance). True if fee is for regulated debit, false otherwise.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this fee schedule expires or is superseded. Null for currently active fee schedules with no defined end date.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this fee schedule becomes effective. Used for accurate cost modeling across time periods.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_code
attributes.description: Scheme-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this fee within the scheme's fee schedule.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the fee is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: fee_description

attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_fixed_amount
attributes.description: Fixed fee amount per transaction in the fee currency. Null if fee is not fixed-amount-based.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the specific fee as published by the card scheme (e.g., 'Visa Assessment Fee', 'Mastercard Cross-Border Volume Fee', 'Amex Digital Enablement Fee').
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage rate applied to transaction value, expressed as decimal (e.g., 0.00125 for 12.5 basis points). Null if fee is not percentage-based.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_rate_type
attributes.description: Structure of the fee calculation: percentage (basis points of transaction value), fixed (flat amount per transaction), tiered (volume-based brackets), or hybrid (combination).
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fee schedule: active (currently in effect), pending (announced but not yet effective), superseded (replaced by newer schedule), or retired (no longer applicable).
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: fee_type
attributes.description: Category of scheme fee: assessment (volume-based), network access (fixed connectivity), cross-border (international transaction), digital enablement (tokenization/digital wallet), misuse-of-authorization (declined auth reuse), or scheme-specific surcharge.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this scheme fee table record was last updated, reflecting any changes to fee rates, effective dates, or other attributes.

attributes.name: maximum_fee_amount
attributes.description: Maximum fee amount charged per transaction, capping percentage-based fees for high-value transactions.
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: mcc_range_high
attributes.description: Upper bound of MCC range to which this fee applies. Used for merchant-category-specific fees. Null if fee applies to all MCCs.
attributes.references: ISO 18245; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: mcc_range_low
attributes.description: Lower bound of MCC range to which this fee applies. Used for merchant-category-specific fees. Null if fee applies to all MCCs.
attributes.references: ISO 18245; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: Minimum fee amount charged per transaction, regardless of percentage calculation. Ensures floor for low-value transactions.

attributes.name: party_type
attributes.description: Indicates which party in the payment chain is charged this fee: acquirer (merchant's bank), issuer (cardholder's bank), or both.

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or region code where this fee applies (e.g., USA, GBR, EUR for Eurozone). Null if fee is global.

attributes.name: scheme_publication_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the official scheme publication, bulletin, or rules document where this fee is defined (e.g., 'Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees April 2024').
attributes.references: Visa Product and Service Rules; Mastercard Standards and Compliance

attributes.name: three_d_secure_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee applies to transactions authenticated via 3-D Secure protocol (3DS 1.0 or 3DS 2.0). True if 3DS-specific, false otherwise.

attributes.name: transaction_type
attributes.description: Type of transaction to which this fee applies: purchase, cash advance, refund, chargeback, or all transaction types.

products.name: bin_interchange_rule
products.description: BIN (Bank Identification Number) level interchange qualification rules mapping BIN ranges to applicable interchange rate categories. Captures BIN range start/end, issuing bank identifier, card product type (debit, credit, prepaid, commercial), regulated/unregulated flag under Durbin Amendment, applicable IRF category codes, and scheme identifier. Core to real-time interchange qualification during transaction processing.

attributes.name: bin_interchange_rule_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bank Identification Number (BIN) Interchange Rule ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate primary key identifying a BIN-level interchange qualification rule record in the silver layer lakehouse. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a configuration/rule resource governing interchange qualification for a BIN range.

attributes.name: card_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.card_program. Business justification: BIN-based interchange rules determine rates for specific card programs (rewards, corporate, prepaid). Issuers configure interchange eligibility by card program. Critical for interchange qualification

attributes.name: currency_pair_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.currency_pair. Business justification: BIN-level interchange rules define eligible currency pairs for cross-border routing and rate application. Required for BIN-based currency eligibility validation and cross-border transaction routing de

attributes.name: ecosystem_partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the issuing bank or financial institution that issued the card associated with this BIN range. The issuing bank is the cardholder's bank in the payment chain.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II

attributes.name: irf_rate_category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interchange.irf_rate_category. Business justification: bin_interchange_rule references IRF category; adds irf_rate_category_id FK

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interchange.program. Business justification: bin_interchange_rule.scheme_program_code (STRING) stores the card scheme program code that governs the BIN-level interchange qualification rule (e.g., Visa CPS, Mastercard Merit). The program product

attributes.name: risk_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_profile. Business justification: BIN-level interchange rules are risk-segmented by issuer. Issuer risk profiles determine rule applicability, rate eligibility, and Durbin regulation status. Critical for issuer onboarding and rate tab

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Reference to the card scheme (payment network brand) governing this interchange rule, such as Visa, Mastercard, American Express, or Discover. Links to the scheme reference product.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo

attributes.name: superseded_by_rule_bin_interchange_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the bin_interchange_rule_id of the newer rule that supersedes this record when rule_status is 'superseded'. Enables rule lineage tracking and historical interchange qualification reconstruction.
attributes.references: SOX; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: authorization_indicator
attributes.description: Specifies the type of authorization associated with this interchange rule: pre-authorization (hotel/car rental), final authorization, or incremental authorization. Different authorization types may qualify for distinct interchange rates.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: avs_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether Address Verification System (AVS) check is required for a transaction to qualify for this interchange rate category. AVS validation is a fraud prevention measure commonly required for card-not-present interchange qualification.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: bin_range_end
attributes.description: The ending BIN (Bank Identification Number) of the BIN range to which this interchange qualification rule applies. Together with bin_range_start, defines the full BIN range covered by this rule.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 7812; PCI DSS v4.0; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: bin_range_start
attributes.description: The starting BIN (Bank Identification Number), also known as IIN (Issuer Identification Number), of the BIN range to which this interchange qualification rule applies. Supports 6-digit legacy BINs and 8-digit extended BINs per ISO/IEC 7812.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 7812; PCI DSS v4.0; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: card_not_present_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies to card-not-present (CNP) transactions, such as e-commerce, mail order, or telephone order (MOTO) transactions. CNP transactions typically carry higher interchange rates due to elevated fraud risk.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: card_present_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies to card-present (CP) transactions, where the physical card or device is used at a POS or mPOS terminal. Card-present transactions typically qualify for lower interchange rates than card-not-present.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; EMVCo EMV Chip Specifications

attributes.name: contactless_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies to contactless NFC (Near Field Communication) transactions, including tap-to-pay and mobile wallet payments. Contactless qualification may carry distinct interchange rates from contact chip transactions.
attributes.references: EMVCo Contactless Specifications; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; NFC Forum

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the issuing country associated with this BIN range (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU). Determines domestic vs. cross-border interchange rate applicability and regulatory jurisdiction.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; GDPR; PSD2

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this BIN interchange rule record was first created in the data platform. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED field for audit trail and data lineage purposes. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX; GDPR Article 5; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: cross_border_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies specifically to cross-border transactions where the issuing country differs from the acquiring country. Cross-border transactions typically attract higher interchange rates and additional scheme fees.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PSD2; SWIFT

attributes.name: data_quality_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates the level of transaction data (Level 1, Level 2, Level 3) required for interchange qualification under this rule. Level 2/3 data (enhanced transaction detail for B2B/commercial cards) may qualify for lower interchange rates.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: durbin_exempt_reason
attributes.description: Reason code explaining why a BIN range is exempt from Durbin Amendment regulated interchange caps. Applicable only when durbin_regulated_flag is False. Small issuers (assets < $10B), government-administered programs, and certain prepaid products qualify for exemption.
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Regulation II (Durbin Amendment); Dodd-Frank Act Section 1075; CFPB

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this BIN range is subject to the Durbin Amendment interchange fee caps under Federal Reserve Regulation II. True = regulated (issuer assets ≥ $10B threshold, capped at 21 cents + 0.05% + 1 cent fraud adjustment); False = unregulated (exempt issuers, higher interchange applies).
attributes.references: Federal Reserve Regulation II (Durbin Amendment); Dodd-Frank Act Section 1075

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this BIN interchange qualification rule ceases to be effective. Null indicates an open-ended rule with no defined expiry. Used to manage rule versioning and historical interchange cost analysis. Serves as EFFECTIVE_UNTIL for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this BIN interchange qualification rule becomes effective and is applied during transaction processing and interchange qualification. Aligns with scheme fee schedule publication cycles (typically semi-annual for Visa/Mastercard). Serves as EFFECTIVE_FROM for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II

attributes.name: emv_chip_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether EMV (Europay Mastercard Visa) chip processing is required for a transaction to qualify for this interchange rate category. EMV chip transactions reduce fraud liability and may qualify for preferential interchange rates.
attributes.references: EMVCo EMV Chip Specifications; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: installment_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies to installment payment transactions, including BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later) arrangements. Installment transactions may carry distinct interchange qualification criteria.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; CFPB

attributes.name: interchange_fee_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the interchange fixed fee is denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for cross-border interchange cost calculations and multi-currency acquiring portfolios.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: interchange_fixed_fee
attributes.description: The fixed per-transaction fee component of the interchange, expressed in the applicable currency (e.g., 0.1000 = $0.10 per transaction). Combined with interchange_rate_percent to compute total interchange cost per transaction.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II

attributes.name: interchange_rate_percent
attributes.description: The percentage-based component of the interchange fee applied to the transaction amount for qualifying transactions under this BIN rule (e.g., 1.6500 represents 1.65%). Used in cost-of-acceptance calculations for acquiring portfolios. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation II; SOX

attributes.name: mcc_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of MCC (Merchant Category Code) values that are included or excluded from this interchange rule, as determined by mcc_restriction_type. For example, '5411,5412,5499' for grocery MCCs. Null when mcc_restriction_type is 'all'.
attributes.references: ISO 18245 (MCC Standard); Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: mcc_restriction_type
attributes.description: Defines how MCC (Merchant Category Code) restrictions apply to this interchange rule: 'all' means no MCC restriction (applies to all MCCs), 'include' means only specified MCCs qualify, 'exclude' means specified MCCs are excluded, 'none' means no transactions qualify regardless of MCC.
attributes.references: ISO 18245 (MCC Standard); Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: recurring_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interchange rule applies to recurring or subscription-based transactions. Recurring transactions may qualify for specific interchange programs with distinct rate structures.

attributes.name: region_code
attributes.description: Card scheme-defined geographic region code associated with this BIN range (e.g., 'AP' for Asia Pacific, 'CEMEA' for Central Europe Middle East Africa, 'LAC' for Latin America and Caribbean, 'NA' for North America). Used for cross-border interchange rate determination.

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business code identifying this BIN interchange qualification rule, used in downstream transaction processing and interchange qualification engines. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: rule_description
attributes.description: Free-text description providing additional context about this BIN interchange qualification rule, including any special conditions, exceptions, or notes from the card scheme or compliance team.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the BIN interchange qualification rule (e.g., 'Visa Debit Regulated CPS Retail'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this BIN interchange qualification rule. Active rules are applied in real-time interchange qualification; superseded rules have been replaced by newer versions; expired rules are past their effective end date. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE entity.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; SOX

attributes.name: source_system_rule_ref
attributes.description: The native rule identifier or reference code from the originating operational system (Transaction Processing Platform or Payment Gateway) from which this BIN interchange rule was sourced. Supports data lineage and reconciliation back to the system of record.

attributes.name: three_ds_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether 3-D Secure (3DS) authentication is required for card-not-present transactions to qualify for this interchange rate. 3DS-authenticated transactions may qualify for lower interchange rates and shift fraud liability to the issuer. Relevant under PSD2 SCA requirements.
attributes.references: EMVCo 3-D Secure Specification; PSD2 Article 97 (SCA); Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: tokenization_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether transactions using a DPAN (Device Primary Account Number) or network token issued by a TSP (Token Service Provider) for this BIN range are eligible for this interchange rate. Tokenized transactions may qualify for distinct interchange rates.
attributes.references: EMVCo Tokenization Framework; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: transaction_max_amount
attributes.description: Maximum transaction amount (in the fee currency) eligible for this interchange rate category. Transactions exceeding this threshold may be subject to different interchange rates or require additional qualification criteria.

attributes.name: transaction_min_amount
attributes.description: Minimum transaction amount (in the fee currency) required for a transaction to qualify for this interchange rate category. Transactions below this threshold may downgrade to a less favorable interchange tier.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this BIN interchange rule record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, rule versioning audit, and regulatory compliance reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: SOX; GDPR Article 5; PCI DSS v4.0

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this BIN interchange rule record, incremented each time the rule is updated. Supports rule versioning and historical interchange qualification audit trails required for regulatory compliance and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: SOX; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.description: Reference to the cleared transaction for which interchange qualification was performed. Links to the transaction processing platform record.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Unique 23-digit acquirer reference number assigned to the transaction by the acquiring bank. Used for transaction tracing across the payment network.

attributes.name: authorization_date
attributes.description: Date on which the transaction was authorized. Time between authorization and settlement is a factor in interchange qualification.

attributes.name: avs_result_code
attributes.description: Result code from address verification system check performed during authorization. AVS match is a qualifying criterion for many card-not-present interchange categories.

attributes.name: bin
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bank Identification Number (BIN) / Issuer Identification Number (IIN)
attributes.description: First 6-8 digits of the card number identifying the issuing bank and card program. BIN-level interchange qualification rules determine which IRF category applies based on issuer and card product.

attributes.name: card_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction was card-present (face-to-face) or card-not-present (e-commerce, mail order, phone order). Card-present transactions typically qualify for lower interchange rates.

attributes.name: contactless_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction was processed using contactless NFC technology (tap-to-pay). Contactless transactions may qualify for specific interchange categories.

attributes.name: cross_border_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction crossed international borders (acquiring country differs from issuing country). Cross-border transactions typically incur higher interchange rates and additional scheme fees.

attributes.name: cvv_result_code
attributes.description: Result code from CVV verification performed during authorization. CVV match is a qualifying criterion for card-not-present transactions to achieve optimal interchange rates.

attributes.name: downgrade_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating why the transaction was downgraded to a higher interchange rate category. Null if transaction qualified for optimal rate. Common reasons include missing AVS, non-EMV, delayed settlement, or missing Level 2/3 data.

attributes.name: downgrade_reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of why the transaction was downgraded, providing detail on the specific qualification criteria that were not met.

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction is subject to Durbin Amendment interchange rate caps (applies to debit cards issued by banks with $10B+ in assets in the United States). Durbin-regulated transactions have capped interchange rates.

attributes.name: emv_chip_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction was processed using EMV chip technology. EMV transactions typically qualify for preferential interchange rates due to enhanced security.

attributes.name: interchange_amount
attributes.description: The total calculated interchange fee amount for this transaction based on the qualified IRF rate and transaction amount. This is the fee paid from the acquiring bank to the issuing bank.

attributes.name: irf_fixed_amount
attributes.description: The fixed fee component of the qualified interchange fee applied to the transaction. Expressed in the settlement currency.
attributes.references: Visa Interchange Reimbursement Fees, Mastercard Interchange Programs

attributes.name: irf_rate_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage rate component of the qualified interchange fee applied to the transaction amount. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0175 for 1.75%).
attributes.references: Visa Interchange Reimbursement Fees, Mastercard Interchange Programs

attributes.name: level_2_data_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Level 2 enhanced data (tax amount, customer code, etc.) was provided with the transaction. Level 2 data is required for commercial card interchange optimization.
attributes.references: Visa Commercial Solutions, Mastercard Business Solutions

attributes.name: level_3_data_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Level 3 line-item data (item descriptions, quantities, unit costs) was provided with the transaction. Level 3 data is required for optimal commercial and purchasing card interchange rates.
attributes.references: Visa Commercial Solutions, Mastercard Business Solutions

attributes.name: qualification_status
attributes.description: Status indicating whether the transaction qualified for the optimal interchange rate, was downgraded to a higher-cost tier, is exempt from interchange, or encountered an error during qualification.

attributes.name: qualification_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the interchange qualification process was executed and the IRF category was determined. Represents the business event time of qualification.

attributes.name: settlement_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the interchange amount is settled between acquiring and issuing banks.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the transaction was settled and interchange fees were calculated and transferred between acquiring and issuing banks. Delayed settlement can result in interchange downgrades.

attributes.name: three_ds_authentication_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transaction was authenticated using 3-D Secure protocol (Verified by Visa, Mastercard SecureCode). 3DS authentication is a qualifying criterion for e-commerce interchange optimization.
attributes.references: EMVCo 3-D Secure Specifications, PSD2 SCA Requirements

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: The gross transaction amount on which the interchange fee was calculated. Expressed in the transaction currency before any currency conversion.

attributes.name: transaction_currency_code

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.description: The date and time when this downgrade record was first created in the data platform.

attributes.name: cvv_response_code
attributes.description: Code returned by the issuer indicating the result of CVV verification, which is often required for optimal interchange qualification in card-not-present transactions.

attributes.name: detected_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the interchange downgrade was identified and recorded in the system.

attributes.name: downgraded_irf_rate_bps
attributes.business_glossary_term: Downgraded Interchange Reimbursement Fee (IRF) Rate in Basis Points
attributes.description: The actual interchange rate in basis points applied after the downgrade, representing a higher cost to the merchant.

attributes.name: durbin_regulated_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the transaction is subject to Durbin Amendment interchange rate caps for regulated debit cards.

attributes.name: emv_chip_transaction
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the transaction used EMV chip technology, which typically qualifies for lower interchange rates.

attributes.name: incremental_cost_amount
attributes.description: The additional interchange fee cost incurred by the merchant due to the downgrade, calculated as the rate differential applied to the transaction amount.

attributes.name: incremental_cost_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the incremental cost amount.

attributes.name: mcc
attributes.description: Four-digit code classifying the merchant's type of business, which influences interchange qualification rules.

attributes.name: merchant_processing_channel
attributes.description: The channel through which the transaction was processed, affecting interchange qualification criteria.

attributes.name: original_irf_rate_bps
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Interchange Reimbursement Fee (IRF) Rate in Basis Points
attributes.description: The optimal interchange rate in basis points that would have applied if the transaction had not been downgraded.

attributes.name: preventable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the downgrade could have been prevented through merchant action or system configuration changes.

attributes.name: rate_differential_bps
attributes.description: The difference in basis points between the downgraded rate and the original qualified rate, representing the incremental cost penalty.

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the specific reason for the interchange downgrade, such as missing AVS data, late settlement, or incomplete transaction data.

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Human-readable explanation of why the transaction was downgraded, providing context for merchant coaching and remediation.

attributes.name: remediation_action_recommended
attributes.description: Suggested corrective action for the merchant to prevent future downgrades of this type, used for merchant coaching and optimization.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the transaction was settled and the downgrade was applied during clearing.

attributes.name: settlement_delay_days
attributes.description: Number of days between authorization and settlement, where excessive delay can trigger interchange downgrades.

attributes.name: three_ds_authentication_status
attributes.description: Status of 3-D Secure authentication for the transaction, which can affect interchange qualification for e-commerce transactions.

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: The gross transaction amount in the transaction currency on which the interchange fees are calculated.

attributes.name: transaction_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction amount.

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The date on which the original transaction was authorized or processed.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this downgrade record was last modified in the data platform.

products.name: scheme_invoice

attributes.name: participant_id

attributes.name: payable_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to ledger.payable. Business justification: Scheme invoices become payables in the ledger - natural accounts payable workflow. Links scheme billing to AP processing, payment scheduling, and cash management.

attributes.name: rate_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fx.fx_rate. Business justification: Scheme invoices may be issued in various currencies; linking to the FX rate enables accurate accounting and audit of converted totals.

attributes.name: scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Scheme invoices are issued by specific card schemes for network participation, assessment, and service fees. Accounts payable reconciliation, scheme fee dispute management, and regulatory reporting al

attributes.name: settlement_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to settlement.settlement_account. Business justification: Scheme invoices are paid from/to designated settlement accounts. The payment of scheme fees requires knowing which settlement account is debited/credited — a core treasury and scheme fee payment opera

attributes.name: settlement_cycle_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to settlement.cycle. Business justification: Links scheme invoices to the settlement cycle they belong to, supporting regulatory reporting of scheme fees per cycle.

attributes.name: adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The net amount of credits, refunds, or additional charges applied to this invoice as adjustments from prior billing periods or corrections. Positive values represent additional charges; negative values represent credits.

attributes.name: assessment_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing assessment fees charged by the card scheme based on transaction volume or value. Typically calculated as a percentage of Total Payment Volume (TPV) or Gross Merchandise Value (GMV).

attributes.name: billing_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the billing period covered by this scheme invoice. Defines the end of the time window for which fees and assessments are being charged.

attributes.name: billing_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the billing period covered by this scheme invoice. Defines the beginning of the time window for which fees and assessments are being charged.

attributes.name: chargeback_processing_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing fees charged by the card scheme for processing chargebacks and disputes during the billing period. Includes fees for dispute lifecycle management and arbitration services.

attributes.name: compliance_penalty_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing penalties or fines assessed by the card scheme for non-compliance with network rules, PCI DSS requirements, or other regulatory standards. Zero if no penalties were assessed.

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: The cost center or business unit code responsible for this scheme invoice expense. Used for internal cost allocation and management reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scheme invoice record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: cross_border_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing fees charged for cross-border or international transactions where the issuing bank and acquiring bank are in different countries or regions.

attributes.name: dispute_date
attributes.description: The date on which this invoice was formally disputed with the card scheme. Null if invoice has not been disputed.

attributes.name: dispute_reason_code
attributes.description: The reason code provided if this invoice is disputed. Indicates the nature of the dispute (e.g., incorrect fee calculation, unrecognized charges, billing error). Null if invoice is not disputed.

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the dispute for this invoice was resolved. Null if dispute is still open or if invoice was never disputed.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The date by which payment must be received by the card scheme to avoid late fees or penalties. Defines the payment deadline for this invoice.

attributes.name: interchange_reimbursement_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing Interchange Reimbursement Fees (IRF) paid between acquiring and issuing banks through the card scheme. This is the fee paid by the acquiring bank to the issuing bank for each transaction.

attributes.name: invoice_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which this scheme invoice is denominated. All monetary amounts on this invoice are expressed in this currency.

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: The date on which the card scheme issued this invoice. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the billing statement was generated and sent.

attributes.name: invoice_document_url
attributes.description: The URL or file path to the original invoice document (PDF or other format) provided by the card scheme. Used for audit trail and detailed line-item review.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The externally-known unique invoice number assigned by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) for this billing statement. This is the business identifier used for reconciliation and payment reference.

attributes.name: invoice_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the scheme invoice indicating its payment and processing state. Tracks the invoice from issuance through payment completion or dispute resolution.

attributes.name: network_participation_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing fees charged for participation in the card scheme network. This is a recurring membership or access fee for being part of the payment network.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments related to this scheme invoice, including special instructions, dispute details, or reconciliation observations. Used for operational communication and audit trail.

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which payment was made to the card scheme for this invoice. Null if invoice remains unpaid.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: The payment instrument or method used to settle this scheme invoice. Indicates how the payment was made to the card scheme.

attributes.name: payment_reference_number
attributes.description: The unique reference number or transaction identifier for the payment made to settle this invoice. Used for payment reconciliation and audit trail. Null if invoice is unpaid.

attributes.name: reconciliation_reference
attributes.description: The reference identifier linking this scheme invoice to the internal reconciliation record or general ledger entry. Used to track the invoice through the accounts payable and financial close process.

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: The current status of the reconciliation process for this scheme invoice, indicating whether the invoice has been matched to internal transaction records and general ledger entries.

attributes.name: scheme_service_fee_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the invoice representing fees for specific card scheme services such as tokenization, fraud prevention, dispute resolution, or other value-added services provided by the network.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of taxes (VAT, GST, sales tax, or other applicable taxes) applied to this scheme invoice. Zero if no taxes are applicable.

attributes.name: total_amount_due
attributes.description: The total amount payable to the card scheme for this invoice, representing the sum of all line-item fees, assessments, and charges. This is the net total amount due before any adjustments or credits.

attributes.name: transaction_value
attributes.description: The total monetary value of all transactions processed through the card scheme network during the billing period, expressed in the invoice currency. Represents the Total Payment Volume (TPV) or Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) for fee calculation purposes.

attributes.name: transaction_volume
attributes.description: The total number of transactions processed through the card scheme network during the billing period covered by this invoice. Used to validate volume-based fee calculations.

attributes.name: updated_by
attributes.description: The user ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified this scheme invoice record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this scheme invoice record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to interchange.program. Business justification: cross_border_fee_rule.scheme_program_code (STRING) stores the card scheme program code associated with the cross-border fee rule (e.g., a specific Visa or Mastercard cross-border program). The program

attributes.name: card_present_indicator

attributes.name: originating_region_code

attributes.name: priority_rank

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.payment_product. Business justification: Chargeback performance dashboard requires product‑level metrics for risk analysis and scheme reporting; linking each chargeback to its payment_product enables this.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to network.scheme. Business justification: Chargebacks are filed under a specific card scheme; scheme_id enables scheme‑level chargeback reporting required by Visa/Mastercard compliance.

attributes.name: settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to settlement.settlement. Business justification: Chargeback settlement reports must link to the settlement record that includes the chargeback amount for traceability.

attributes.description: Reference to the originating payment transaction record in the transaction domain that is the subject of this chargeback filing. Links the chargeback to the full transaction detail including authorization, capture, and settlement data.

attributes.description: Net financial adjustment amount posted to the merchant's account as a result of this chargeback. Negative value indicates a debit to the merchant; positive value indicates a credit (e.g., upon successful representment).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: Gross amount of the chargeback as filed by the issuing bank in the transaction currency. Represents the disputed amount that will be debited from the merchant's account if the chargeback is upheld. May differ from the original transaction amount in cases of partial chargebacks.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 4217; ERP - Oracle Financials

attributes.name: arbitration_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline for filing an arbitration case with the card scheme after a failed pre-arbitration or second chargeback cycle. Arbitration is the final escalation path where the card scheme adjudicates the dispute and assigns liability. Missing this deadline forfeits the right to arbitration.

attributes.name: arbitration_filing_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the arbitration case was filed with the card scheme. Populated only when the chargeback has been escalated to the arbitration stage (cycle_stage = ARBITRATION).

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: Acquirer Reference Number uniquely identifying the originating payment transaction across the card scheme network. Primary linkage key between the chargeback and the settled transaction. Assigned by the acquiring bank at settlement and used by all parties to trace the transaction through the payment chain.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: card_scheme
attributes.description: Payment network brand (card scheme) under whose rules this chargeback is governed. Determines the applicable reason code taxonomy, response deadlines, cycle stages, and arbitration procedures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: VISA|MASTERCARD|AMEX|DISCOVER|UNIONPAY|OTHER — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules; EMVCo

attributes.name: cardholder_dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the cardholder's stated reason for disputing the transaction as captured by the issuing bank. Provides the narrative context behind the formal reason code classification. Used by the merchant in preparing the representment package.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; CFPB Regulation E

attributes.name: case_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the chargeback case as assigned by the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Used by operations teams, merchants, and card schemes to reference the chargeback in correspondence, representment packages, and scheme portal submissions.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: chargeback_status
attributes.description: Current disposition and lifecycle status of the chargeback record. Tracks the chargeback from initial receipt through final resolution. RECEIVED: chargeback filed by issuer; UNDER_REVIEW: internal review in progress; AWAITING_RESPONSE: merchant response pending; REPRESENTED: merchant submitted representment; ACCEPTED: merchant accepted liability; WON: merchant successfully defended; LOST: chargeback upheld; ARBITRATION: escalated to scheme arbitration; CLOSED: final resolution reached. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: RECEIVED|UNDER_REVIEW|AWAITING_RESPONSE|REPRESENTED|ACCEPTED|WON|LOST|ARBITRATION|CLOSED — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chargeback record was first created in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System (Silver Layer). Represents the system ingestion time, distinct from the filing_timestamp which is the business event time when the issuer filed the chargeback with the card scheme.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR Article 5; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the chargeback amount is denominated. May differ from the original transaction currency in cross-border disputes where Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) was applied.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: cycle_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the chargeback lifecycle cycle as defined by card scheme rules. FIRST_CHARGEBACK is the initial filing by the issuer; SECOND_CHARGEBACK (also called pre-arbitration chargeback under Mastercard rules) occurs after a failed representment; PRE_ARBITRATION is the Visa pre-arbitration stage; ARBITRATION is the final scheme-level adjudication; COMPLIANCE is a scheme compliance filing.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines

attributes.name: deadline_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the chargeback response was submitted on or before the scheme-mandated response deadline. True if response_timestamp is on or before response_deadline; False if the deadline was missed, resulting in automatic acceptance of the chargeback liability.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: evidence_package_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the evidence package (representment documentation) submitted by the merchant to contest the chargeback. Points to the document management system location containing delivery confirmations, signed receipts, authorization records, and other supporting evidence.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: filing_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal business event timestamp recording when the chargeback was formally filed by the issuing bank with the card scheme. This is the scheme-recognized filing date used to calculate all response deadlines and compliance windows per card scheme rules.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583; Regulation E (Federal Reserve)

attributes.name: fraud_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback is classified as fraud-related based on the reason code category (True) or non-fraud (False). Fraud chargebacks (e.g., Visa reason code 10.x, Mastercard reason code 4837/4863) are tracked separately for fraud reporting, chargeback ratio monitoring, and Fraud Detection and Prevention Platform feedback loops.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS; FinCEN BSA

attributes.name: is_partial_chargeback
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback is for a partial amount of the original transaction (True) or for the full transaction amount (False). Partial chargebacks occur when only a portion of the goods or services are disputed.

attributes.name: liability_party
attributes.description: The party determined to bear financial liability for the chargeback upon final resolution. MERCHANT: merchant absorbs the loss; ISSUER: issuing bank absorbs the loss; ACQUIRER: acquiring bank absorbs the loss; SCHEME: card scheme absorbs the loss (rare, typically in compliance cases).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines

attributes.name: original_transaction_amount
attributes.description: The full amount of the original payment transaction that is the subject of this chargeback, in the original transaction currency. Used to identify partial chargebacks where chargeback_amount is less than the full transaction amount.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; ISO 8583

attributes.name: original_transaction_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the currency in which the original payment transaction was denominated. Enables currency reconciliation in cross-border dispute scenarios involving Foreign Exchange (FX) or Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).
attributes.references: ISO 4217; Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules

attributes.name: ratio_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this chargeback has been flagged as contributing to the merchant's chargeback ratio threshold breach under card scheme monitoring programs (e.g., Visa Chargeback Monitoring Program - VCMP, Mastercard Excessive Chargeback Program - ECP). Merchants exceeding scheme thresholds face fines and potential termination.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; PCI DSS

attributes.name: representment_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline by which the merchant must submit a representment (rebuttal) package to challenge the chargeback. Distinct from response_deadline in that it specifically governs the representment submission window after the merchant elects to contest the chargeback.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: representment_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the merchant submitted the representment package to contest the chargeback. A representment is the merchant's formal response disputing the chargeback, including evidence such as delivery confirmation, signed receipts, or fraud documentation.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: resolution_outcome
attributes.description: Final resolution outcome of the chargeback after all dispute cycles are exhausted. MERCHANT_WON: representment was successful and chargeback reversed; ISSUER_WON: chargeback upheld and merchant debited; SPLIT_LIABILITY: liability shared between parties; WITHDRAWN: cardholder or issuer withdrew the dispute; EXPIRED: chargeback expired due to inaction.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the chargeback reached its final resolution and the case was closed. Marks the end of the chargeback lifecycle. Used for SLA compliance measurement and financial reconciliation timing.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: Scheme-mandated deadline by which the acquiring bank or merchant must submit a representment or accept the chargeback. Calculated from the filing timestamp per card scheme rules (e.g., Visa typically allows 30 calendar days; Mastercard 45 calendar days). Missing this deadline results in automatic chargeback acceptance.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: response_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when the merchant or acquiring bank submitted their response (representment package or acceptance) to the chargeback. Compared against response_deadline to determine deadline compliance status.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

attributes.name: scheme_case_reference
attributes.description: Card scheme-assigned case identifier for the chargeback as provided by Visa, Mastercard, Amex, or Discover through their dispute resolution portals (e.g., Visa Resolve Online - VROL, Mastercard MATCH). Used for scheme-level tracking and arbitration submissions.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: scheme_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fee charged by the card scheme (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover) for processing the chargeback. Scheme fees are assessed per chargeback filing and may vary by scheme, reason code, and merchant chargeback ratio tier. Debited from the acquiring bank and typically passed through to the merchant.
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Amex Chargeback Guidelines; Discover Network Rules

attributes.name: sla_breach
attributes.description: Indicates whether the internal SLA for chargeback processing was breached (True) for this case. Internal SLAs govern the time from chargeback receipt to merchant notification, evidence collection, and representment submission, distinct from the scheme-mandated response deadlines.
attributes.references: Dispute and Chargeback Management System; Internal SLA Policy

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record from which this chargeback record was sourced (e.g., Dispute and Chargeback Management System). Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across the lakehouse architecture.
attributes.references: Data Warehouse and Analytics Platform; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The date on which the original payment transaction that is the subject of this chargeback was processed. Used to verify chargeback filing timeliness against scheme-mandated windows (e.g., Visa allows chargebacks up to 120 days from transaction date in most cases).
attributes.references: Visa Core Rules; Mastercard Rules; Regulation E (Federal Reserve)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the chargeback record in the system. Tracks the last modification across any field in the chargeback lifecycle, supporting audit trail requirements and change detection for downstream data consumers.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR Article 5; Dispute and Chargeback Management System

products.name: retrieval_request
products.description: Pre-chargeback inquiry record issued by an issuing bank requesting transaction documentation (sales draft, receipt, authorization record) from the acquiring bank before a formal chargeback is filed. Tracks retrieval request ID, ARN, MID, TID, request date, fulfillment deadline, fulfillment status, and document delivery method. Failure to fulfill a retrieval request within scheme deadlines typically escalates to a chargeback.

attributes.name: retrieval_request_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the retrieval request record in the Dispute and Chargeback Management System. Primary key for this entity. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: authorization_id
